topic.title: Floyd Mayweather's $100M Equity Stake in a $3B NYC Real Estate Portfolio

selectedHook.hook: Floyd Mayweather just put $100 million into a real estate deal worth $3 billion. That's not because he owns all of it -- it's leverage at a scale most people never see, and the same math applies whether you're investing $10,000 or $100 million.

sourcedFacts.fact: Floyd Mayweather invested $100 million in equity into a joint venture with Go Partners
sourcedFacts.source: CRE Daily; Bisnow; The Real Deal

sourcedFacts.fact: The joint venture's real estate portfolio is valued at about $3 billion
Go Partners is a joint venture between Meyer Orbach (Orbach Affordable Housing Solutions) and Josh Gotlib (Black Spruce Management)
Mayweather's investment vehicle for the deal is Vada Properties, based in Trump Tower in New York City
The portfolio's anchor property is The Copper, twin residential towers (41 and 48 stories) in Murray Hill with 761 units, about 20% of them affordable housing
Go Partners bought The Copper for $850 million in 2021

The rest of the portfolio -- properties from the late Sheldon Solow's holdings, including One and Two Sutton Place North, One East River Place, 265 East 66th Street, and 685 First Avenue -- was assembled for about $1.7 billion between late 2022 and April 2023
Mayweather earned $560 million over his undefeated professional boxing career
Mayweather's specific ownership percentage in the joint venture has not been publicly disclosed

sourcedFacts.fact: $100 million is approximately 3.3% of a $3 billion portfolio

workingTitle: The Real Math Behind Floyd Mayweather's $3 Billion Real Estate Stake

beats.line: Floyd Mayweather just put $100 million into a real estate deal worth $3 billion.
$100 million into a $3 billion portfolio — that's not because he owns all of it. It's leverage at a scale most people never see.
The deal is a joint venture with Go Partners — real estate investors Meyer Orbach and Josh Gotlib — through Mayweather's own firm, Vada Properties.
The portfolio's anchor is The Copper, twin towers in Murray Hill with 761 units — bought for $850 million in 2021.
The rest came from the late Sheldon Solow's holdings — four more Manhattan buildings assembled for about $1.7 billion.
Combined, that's a $3 billion portfolio of New York City real estate.
$100 million is about 3% of that total. The other 97% comes from other equity partners and mortgage debt on the properties themselves.
That's the same leverage principle behind a $20,000 down payment on a $400,000 house — just multiplied to an institutional scale.
Mayweather earned $560 million across his undefeated boxing career — real estate is how he's putting a fraction of that to work.
His exact ownership stake in the joint venture has never been made public — only the $100 million contribution and the portfolio's total value.
$100 million in. $3 billion portfolio. Roughly 3% of the total — the rest is leverage, not personal cash.
You don't need $100 million to use this. Understanding how equity partners and debt combine is what lets any investor control more than their own cash could buy.

factCheckWarnings: Mayweather's exact ownership percentage in the Go Partners JV is not publicly disclosed -- the script only states his $100M contribution and the portfolio's $3B total value, and explicitly flags the ownership stake as undisclosed (beat 10) rather than implying he owns 3% of the equity or any other specific share.
